items.label: 1A
items.claim: GEO human NovaSeq X share of 6000+X series has risen about 1.3 points a quarter since Q3'24 and has not flattened.
items.why_new: This is a full 11-quarter series count and fitted slope; earlier items gave only isolated points (F692: 35/123/251) or sample-based shares.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Extending the linear trend puts the human X series share near 19% by Q4'27, a gain of about 5.4 points over calendar 2027.
items.detail: The fit is y=7.24+1.345*(t-4). Q4'26 (t=9) is 13.97% and Q4'27 (t=13) is 19.35%, so the 2027 gain is 5.4 pts. That is close to the thesis's roughly 5 points of 2027 mix shift. The fit is linear, so a logistic curve would give a similar or slightly faster path at these low levels. The caveat is that this is a share of published series, a lagging proxy, and it is not a Gb or revenue share.
items.why_new: This is the first projection of the 2027 pace of conversion from public data, and it lands on the thesis's 5-point figure.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Outside China and the EU/Japan list (mostly US-led), the X share of series jumped from about 10% to about 17.5% in a year.
items.detail: Residual cohort = all minus China minus EU/Japan. Q3'26: 6000 1647-438-145=1064, X 251-8-18=225, share 225/1289=17.5%. Q3'25: 6000 1441-362-168=911, X 123-4-14=105, share 105/1016=10.3%. That is +7.2 pts a year. Continuing it five quarters gives about 26% by Q4'27, which is faster than the global fit. The cohort is a residual, not a clean US list.
items.source_name: NCBI GEO via E-utilities; derived by subtraction
items.why_new: This gives a cohort-level slope, where F696 gave only a share for ten named US institutions.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: The EU/Japan institution list is converting at about +3.3 points a year, slower than the rest of the world.
items.detail: For a list of Japan, Germany, France, Karolinska, Oxford, Cambridge, Tokyo and Munich, X series were 18 against 145 6000 series in Q3'26, a share of 11.0%. In Q3'25 it was 14 against 168, 7.7%. The 6000 count there fell 14% y/y while the X count rose 29%. A keyword list is only a proxy for country, and the list is not the T591/T588 cohort.
items.why_new: No earlier item gives a regional X-share slope.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: China-institution series are still almost entirely on the 6000, and the 6000 count there rose 21% y/y.
items.detail: China[INST] 6000 series were 438 in Q3'26 against 362 in Q3'25 (+21%). X series were 8 against 4. The X share was 1.8% against 1.1%, so the gain is +0.7 pts a year. China is about 27% of all human 6000 series (438/1647). That group is a large block with almost no conversion, which fits a tail that stays on the 6000. Chinese import restrictions likely explain this, so it is not a clinical-tail signal.
items.why_new: F695 gave only zero-X for ten institutions; this gives the China series counts and a y/y slope.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Absolute human 6000 series counts are not shrinking, so the share gain comes from X growth on top of a flat to rising 6000 base.
items.detail: 6000 series per quarter were 1342, 1485, 1380, 1392, 1522, 1460, 1441, 1340, 1837, 1408 and 1647 from Q1'24 to Q3'26. Q3'26 is +14% y/y against Q3'25 and the series is noisy, with a Q1'26 spike. X series are growing 2x y/y (123 to 251) on a much smaller base. A 6000 share that falls by 1.3 pts a quarter while 6000 output stays flat is a weak sign of tail erosion.
items.why_new: This gives the full quarterly 6000 series line; earlier items cited only Q3 comparisons (F580).

notes: Mouse 6000/X GPLs, HiSeq/NextSeq, and AVITI/UG100/T7 series per quarter were not run; the tool budget went to the 22-call human time series. The country proxy for the US failed. My US-institution list returned an implausible 18 for Q3'25 6000 series against 262 in Q3'26, so I dropped it. The 'rest of world' residual replaces it. Counts are series, not Gb, and GEO lags real usage, so the share is a lagging indicator. The country lists are keyword proxies, not the T591/T588 cohorts, which I did not have. Next steps: run the mouse GPLs, GSM counts, and a clean US list. Run Chinese institution X series for 2024-25.
